summary: A reading of American Crusade, the 2020 Christian nationalist manifesto by Fox host and later US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, set against his record of mismanaged veterans groups, Iraq service and a 2017 sexual assault allegation.

evidence.note: host frames the series as a hybrid: mostly reading the 2020 book, plus biographical context
biography starts with his 1980 birth in Minneapolis
Vets for Freedom, PAC and later CVA funds allegedly spent on partying
book invokes the First Crusade and Deus vult; hosts fact-check the medieval history at length
2005 Samarra deployment and the unit's later war crimes case
failed 2012 Minnesota Senate primary bid as told in the book
segment on pastor Doug Wilson, his church network and theocratic program
book's chapters on Islam as inherently violent, rebutted by the host
account of the 2017 Monterey sexual assault allegation and settlement
follows his later actions up to his 2025 tenure as Secretary of Defense

notes: Hybrid book reading and biography; media-reading wins by precedence. Fascism-far-right chosen as primary per the title; religious-right-culture-war (Christian nationalism) was a close alternative. The First Crusade segment is treated as fact-checking the book, not a subject, so covered_span stays 1980-2025. Afghanistan and Guantanamo service mentioned only briefly.
